speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
text: asked the Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (a) what governance and oversight mechanisms are in place to ensure wakaf assets are managed faithfully in accordance with donors’ intentions while remaining financially sustainable; and (b) how has wakaf management evolved in recent years to address challenges such as fragmented assets, rising maintenance costs, and redevelopment constraints in land-scarce Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There are clear governance mechanisms in place to ensure that wakaf assets remain financially sustainable and are managed with accountability and transparency.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Second, Warees and the appointed mutawallis must comply with audit requirements set out under the AMLA, as well as undergo periodic checks by MUIS that religious guidance by the Fatwa Committee has been adhered to.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Wakaf management has indeed become more challenging over the years.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Amidst rising costs and development needs, MUIS and Warees strive to keep rents affordable, while performing their fiduciary duty to ensure sufficient financial returns for the wakaf beneficiaries.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Where tenants face challenges paying rent, MUIS and Warees engage them to understand their situation and explore repayment plans.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Recent examples include The Red House at East Coast Road and Jamae Chulia Heritage Development at Mosque Street.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MUIS will continue to review and enhance wakaf asset management to ensure that our wakaf assets can sustainably support their intended beneficiaries.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I do appreciate the challenges faced in unlocking the assets and to create greater value.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: In my interactions with members of the Malay/Muslim and the Indian/Muslim community, they have expressed interest to find out how the value from these wakaf assets can be used to uplift the community over time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, we often hear and meet the community leaders, and they ask about such questions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Essentially, the returns from the building rentals, as with any other forms of income generated from the wakaf assets are distributed to beneficiaries in accordance with the wakaf deed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we have to be very clear about that and we follow what is in the wakaf deed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, I have been very fortunate to be involved in the development of wakaf back in the early 2000s, when I was in the MUIS Council, where I was actually looking after the wakaf aspect of MUIS work.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I saw how the community worked together, with MUIS leading the community, to see how the returns go back to where it is supposed to be and to the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Fast forward to today, the Member will see a vast development in that space, whereby, not only have asset or wakaf revitalisation and asset enhancement or optimisation been done, but also looking at the historic value of the wakaf.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: All I can say is that, the community, in fact, has benefited a lot significantly from these wakaf returns.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Sometimes, I discuss with the mosque leaders, community leaders as to how they have been using the returns and I am very happy to see that such returns are something that they look forward to because that helps, not only in how they manage the mosque, but also that helps in the way they reach out to the community and benefit the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, I must say that the returns of wakaf assets not only go back to where it is supposed to be.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But with the value enhancement efforts and the returns that the community has gained have somehow helped to build the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It helps in the development of the Malay/Muslim and Indian/Muslim communities, and beyond.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Also, the Member's second question was about how we engage the community leaders.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, just to give the Member an example, I was also directly involved, I was helping Minister Masagos on the restoration works of the historic Jamae Chulia Mosque and the development and construction of Jamae Chulia Heritage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I remember the various engagement sessions we had.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We tried to reach out to the Indian/Muslim community leaders, had many sessions, even went back and forth when they needed clarity, there were clarifications or even certain things that did not meet the planning criteria.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We spoke to them and then, when there were constraints, we decided on an option that would provide a balanced outcome.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I must say that this process had not only reached, but also gave the community leaders the satisfaction that they are part of this journey.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, this is something that we want to continue to do.
